newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Wireless Data to establish Asia base in Wollongong.
newsitem.headline: Wireless Data to establish Asia base in Wollongong.

text.p: Wireless Data Services, a telecommunications company based in the United Kingdom, announced on Friday a multi-million dollar investment in the regional New South Wales city of Wollongong.

Wireless Data regional director Luke Van Kempen said the company had chosen the city over Singapore because it had cheaper rents, a workforce with language and technical skills and a quality of life which could not be matched elsewhere in the region.

The company, which is a subsidiary of the Hugh Symon Group, would locate its Asia Pacific Regional "call centre" on the campus of the University of Wollongong. Some staff and support engineers would come from the university.
"From today this centre will employ 20 people but its staff will grow quickly to 80, and may reach more than 200 within five years," state government regional development minister Sandra Nori said.
The call centre would assist customers of telecommunication companies such as Telstra, Optus and Nokia when they have trouble sending information via the mobile phone network.
